answer: Merchant jetty co-occurrence scoring. After the fact, the system clusters accounts by the merchants and counterparties they transact with, treating overlap as edges in a bipartite graph. A sybil cluster appears as a dense trellis of shared, rarely used counterparties, flagged when its internal overlap exceeds what independent actors would produce. Enforcement: flagged clusters face graduated withdrawal limits and delayed settlement. The bridge to legitimate use is narrow merchant diversity, which forces an attacker to spread each identity across many distinct counterparties.
